newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu sees copper flat, zinc up slowly.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu sees copper flat, zinc up slowly.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy expects copper prices to remain unchanged in the near future, but zinc to rise gradually over the next few years, Outokumpu CEO Jyrki Juusela said on Monday.
"The copper price is low at the moment. We have no reason to expect any significant improvement, the copper price could rather stay at this level," he told a news conference.
Outokumpu earlier released its eight-month report showing a 108 US cents/lb average copper price in January-August, down from 134 in the first eight months of 1995.
"In zinc, we expect a clear improvement in the long term, in the next few years," he said.
Juusela said nickel could rise but the price outlook was uncertain.
"Nickel is the most difficult to predict. We expect it (the nickel price) to rise somewhat," he said.
The average January-August zinc price remained unchanged at 47 cents/lb, but nickel price fell to $3.52/lb from $3.72 in January-August 1995, Outokumpu said earlier.
Outokumpu showed a 109 million markka profit before extraordinary items and taxes in January-August, down from 1.32 billion markka in the first eight months in 1995.
